title: Care Academy Training Note — Waiting Time and the Price-Protection Limit (Pre-Orders & Back-Orders)
content:
**Rule.** The longer a Pre-Orders & Back-Orders reservation has been held, the more is added to its price-protection limit. The time held is counted in calendar days from the reservation date to today:

- held 60 days or more: adds 3 percentage points (0.03) to the protection limit;
- held 30 days up to fewer than 60 days: adds 1 percentage point (0.01);
- held fewer than 30 days: adds nothing (0.0).

The addition is a share of the reserved unit price, added to the protection limit.

**Questions and answers**

*Which date does the count start from?*
The reservation date on the reservation record. It is counted to today.

*A reservation was made 59 days ago. What is added?*
It falls in the band of 30 up to fewer than 60 days, so 1 percentage point is added.

*And at 60 days?*
Sixty days is "60 days or more", so 3 percentage points are added.

*A reservation made 29 days ago?*
Nothing is added. At 30 days it would gain 1 point.

| Days held | 29 | 30 | 59 | 60 | 95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Added to the protection limit | 0 | 1 point | 1 point | 3 points | 3 points |

*Illustration (hypothetical).* A protection limit of 10 percent on a reservation held 75 days becomes 13 percent of the reserved unit price.
